input.reasoning: Estimation approach: Each backlog item was sized in story points where given; unestimated items were assigned analogous points by comparing complexity to similarly-scoped estimated items (e.g. migration ~13, design system ~8, RBAC ~8, audit log ~5, multi-currency ~8, admin back-office ~8, performance hardening ~5, observability ~5, decommission ~3, support ticket ~5). 1 point ≈ 6 hours of blended engineering effort (a common mid-size-team heuristic), then hours were split across roles per task type (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, integration, infra, data) and QA/DevOps overlay hours were added for testing and pipeline/observability work respectively. Role hour totals were checked against each role's FTE capacity assuming a ~3-month (13-week, ~480 hours/FTE) delivery window: Backend 1.5 FTE ≈ 936h capacity, Frontend 1.0 FTE ≈ 624h, QA 0.6 FTE ≈ 374h, DevOps 0.4 FTE ≈ 250h. Allocations were kept within or close to these envelopes; where the backlog exceeds capacity (notably Backend and QA), this is flagged as an assumption/risk rather than padded. No historical actuals exist for this project, so estimates rely purely on point-based analogy and standard delivery ratios, which increases uncertainty — reflected in the P50/P80/P95 scenario spread. Non-labour costs cover Stripe/webhook sandbox fees, staging infra, legacy Oracle migration tooling/read-replica cost, and email/SMS gateway fees for 2FA and notifications. Priority breakdown sums labour cost per task priority using the same hour allocations. Reductions identify concrete descope/defer opportunities: dropping Low-priority items (support ticket sync, admin back-office, usage analytics, contract tests, legacy decommission) or deferring them to a later phase, trimming accessibility pass scope to critical screens only, and deferring multi-currency to phase 2, each with estimated savings based on their allocated hours.

scenarios.name: P50 - Base case, current scope delivered with assumed sizing accuracy
P80 - Includes typical scope creep, integration friction (Stripe, legacy Oracle migration) and rework
P95 - Includes migration/data quality surprises, security review cycles, and role capacity shortfall requiring extended timeline

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration sandbox/test transaction fees and PCI review support
Staging and CI infrastructure (cloud compute, environments) for PW-1
Legacy Oracle migration tooling, temporary read-replica and data validation licenses (PW-8)
Transactional email/SMS gateway fees for notifications and 2FA enrolment (PW-11, PW-17)
Accessibility audit / WCAG 2.2 AA external review (PW-15)
Contingency for third-party FX rate data feed (PW-14)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project; all effort figures are derived from story-point analogy and standard delivery ratios, not observed velocity.
1 story point is assumed to equal approximately 6 hours of blended engineering effort based on typical mid-complexity SaaS features.

Unestimated tasks were sized by analogy to similarly-scoped estimated tasks (e.g. Legacy data migration ~13pts, Design system ~8pts, RBAC ~8pts, Audit log ~5pts, Multi-currency ~8pts, Admin back-office ~8pts, Performance hardening ~5pts, Observability ~5pts, Support ticket submission ~5pts, Decommission legacy portal ~3pts).
Delivery window assumed at roughly 13 weeks (one quarter), giving approximate capacity of 936 Backend hours, 624 Frontend hours, 374 QA hours and 250 DevOps hours at stated FTE levels.

Backend Developer allocation (980h) slightly exceeds the calculated 1.5 FTE capacity envelope for the assumed timeline, indicating the role is staffed too thinly for the full backlog and either timeline should extend or backend scope should be trimmed.
QA Engineer hours are tightly bound to 0.6 FTE capacity; if all 24 items are tested to full regression depth, QA is undersized and testing may become a bottleneck.
DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) is assumed to only be needed for CI/CD, environment, and observability/rate-limiting tasks rather than continuous full-time engagement.
Non-labour costs are rough market-based placeholders for third-party services (Stripe, email/SMS gateway, migration tooling, accessibility audit, FX data) since no vendor quotes were supplied.

Points-to-hours conversion and role split assumes a typical full-stack feature ratio of roughly 55% backend / 30% frontend / 10% QA overlay / 5% DevOps overlay, adjusted per task nature (e.g., migration is backend+devops heavy, accessibility and responsive layout are frontend+QA heavy).
Priority breakdown allocates labour cost proportionally to the hours estimated per task grouped by its stated priority label.

reductions.description: Descope Low-priority items not essential to MVP launch: Support ticket submission (PW-12), Admin back-office (PW-18), Usage analytics (PW-19), Contract tests against helpdesk (PW-23), Decommission legacy portal (PW-24) — defer all to a post-launch phase 2.
reductions.effect: Removes ~5 backlog items entirely from current scope, reducing Backend, Frontend and QA hours across those tasks.

reductions.description: Defer Multi-currency support (PW-14) to phase 2 since portal can launch USD-only initially.
reductions.effect: Removes backend FX integration and frontend currency display work from current scope.

reductions.description: Narrow Accessibility pass (PW-15) to critical customer journeys (login, dashboard, payment) rather than full WCAG 2.2 AA across all screens for v1.
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend and QA hours allocated to accessibility remediation by roughly half.

reductions.description: Reduce QA Engineer regression scope by adopting risk-based testing (deep coverage only on Urgent/High priority flows, lighter smoke tests on Medium/Low) given the role's limited 0.6 FTE capacity.
reductions.effect: Cuts QA hours on Medium/Low priority items without dropping coverage on payments, auth, and RBAC.

reductions.description: Defer Observability tracing/dashboards (PW-22) beyond payment-path alerting until after initial launch.
reductions.effect: Limits DevOps Engineer scope to only payment-path monitoring now, full tracing/dashboards later.
